name: Sha'ban
intro:
The month of Sha'ban is the month of joy for the Shi'a through the arrival of the Infallible Imams (PBUT). The 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 14th, 15th, 18th and 19th days of this month are important days in the history of Islam.
The births of Imam Husayn (PBUH), Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH), Hadrat Baqiyyatullah al-A'zam (the Imam of the Age), Hadrat Abbas (PBUH) and Hadrat Ali Akbar (PBUH) are the most joyous events of this month. The deaths of Hafsa and Mughira ibn Shu'ba are also two pleasing reports in this month.
On the other hand, the martyrdom of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and the deaths of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri and Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti, two deputies of the Imam of the Age (PBUH), are the days of sorrow of this month.
The war of Banu Sa'd took place in this month. The beginning of the obligation of fasting is a historic day in the field of Islamic rulings. The entry of Imam Husayn (PBUH) into Mecca, the last decree (tawqi') of the Imam of the Age (PBUH) and the introduction of the Imam of the Age (PBUH) to the Shi'a are also the starting points of great developments in the history of Islam.

events.title: Beginning of the Obligation of Fasting
events.text: On this day in the 2nd year AH, fasting in the blessed month of Ramadan became obligatory.
sources: Masar al-Shi'a: p. 37. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 19.

events.title: Death of Mu'tazz the Abbasid
events.text: On this day in the year 255 AH, Mu'tazz Billah went to his doom. His name was Zubayr or Muhammad, and he came to the caliphate after his cousin Musta'in. One of his greatest crimes was that he martyred Imam al-Hadi (PBUH); and because he feared that Mu'ayyad would rise against him, he wrapped him in a poisoned quilt and sealed both its ends until he died on the 23rd of Rajab. He continually killed the commanders of the Turks, until on the day of the Mab'ath (the Prophet's commissioning) in the year 255 AH a group led by Salih ibn Wasif surrounded Mu'tazz, rebuked and reproached him, and demanded money from him. They dragged him out of his chamber and made him stand in the scorching sun, so that from the intensity of the heat he kept shifting his weight onto one foot, and they kept beating him, until on the 27th of Rajab he deposed himself from the caliphate. Then for three days they gave him neither water nor food until he died; according to another account they gave him an enema of boiling water. Some have said: they imprisoned him in a bathhouse for five days without water and food, and on the last day gave him salt water or snow water, and he was killed because of this.
sources: Tatimmat al-Muntaha: pp. 340-343. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 336.

events.title: Birth of Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text: On this day in the year 4 AH, the master of the martyrs, the chief and leader of the Shi'a and those enamored with him, the tear of every believer, the ascetic Imam and worshipper, the lonely martyr, the thirsty one of Naynawa (Nineveh), Hadrat Aba Abdillah al-Husayn al-Shahid (PBUH) illuminated the world with his light. Other views on the date of his birth are the 5th of Sha'ban, the 30th of Rabi' al-Awwal, and the 12th of Rajab.
sources: A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1 p. 420. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 37. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 758. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2 p. 598. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 337. Zad al-Ma'ad: p. 56. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44 pp. 101-202, vol. 94 p. 80, vol. 98 p. 347. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2 p. 3.
Irshad: vol. 2 p. 27. Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2 p. 3.
Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 10. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 226.

subsections.title: Titles of Imam Husayn (PBUH)
subsections.text:
His blessed name is Shabbir in the Torah and Tab in the Gospel. His father is our master and leader, the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), and his mother is Hadrat Waliyyatullah and Habibatuha, the Lady of the Two Abodes, the Truthful One (Siddiqa Kubra), Fatima Zahra (SA).
His kunya is Abu Abdillah, and his special kunya is Abu Ali. His titles are: al-Shahid (the Martyr), al-Sa'id (the Fortunate), al-Sibt al-Thani (the Second Grandson), al-Imam al-Thalith (the Third Imam), al-Rashid (the Rightly Guided), al-Tayyib (the Pure), al-Wafi (the Faithful), al-Sayyid (the Master), al-Zaki (the Pure-hearted), al-Mubarak (the Blessed), and Tabi' li-Mardatillah (the Follower of God's Pleasure).

subsections.title: The Prophet (SAWW) at the Birth of Imam Husayn (PBUH)
subsections.text:
When the news of his birth reached the noble Prophet (SAWW), he came to the house of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) and told Asma to bring the newborn. Asma wrapped him in a white cloth and brought him to the Messenger of God (SAWW). The Prophet (SAWW) recited the adhan in his right ear and the iqama in his left ear.
On the first or seventh day after his birth, Gabriel, the trustworthy angel of revelation, descended and said: “Peace of God be upon you, O Prophet. Name this newborn after the younger son of Aaron, Shabbir, which in Arabic is said Husayn. For Ali (PBUH) is to you as Aaron was to Moses son of Imran, except that you are the Seal of the Prophets.”
In this way the glorious name “Husayn” was chosen by the Lord for the second child of Fatima (SA). On this day the angels of the heavens came to the Prophet (SAWW) to offer congratulations on this birth, and they brought some soil from the grave of this noble one to the Prophet (SAWW) and also offered him condolences.
One of the miracles on the day of his birth was that the angel Futrus (or Dardail) took refuge with this oppressed Imam, and God forgave him and restored him to his former station.
sources: Amali of Shaykh Tusi: vol. 1 p. 377.
Fayd al-'Allam: p. 337. Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 44 p. 182.

subsections.title: The Life of Imam Husayn (PBUH)
subsections.text:
He was with his noble grandfather, the Messenger of God (SAWW), for six years and some months. He lived for thirty years with his honorable father, the Master of the Pious, the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), and took part in the battles of Jamal, Siffin and Nahrawan. During the usurping rule of 'Umar, Imam Husayn (PBUH), at the age of ten, entered the mosque and saw the second caliph speaking from the pulpit of the Prophet (SAWW). He climbed up the pulpit and cried out: “Come down from my father's pulpit!”
After the martyrdom of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), he accompanied and shared in the sufferings of Imam Hasan (PBUH), and witnessed how Mu'awiya and other hypocrites and unbelievers opened their polluted mouths to slander his honorable father, the Commander of the Faithful, and his brother Imam Hasan (PBUH).
After Imam Mujtaba (PBUH) was martyred unjustly, the Imamate passed to that generous being, and after afflictions, harms and taunts, they martyred him on the day of Ashura.
On this day a blessed decree (tawqi') was issued from the Imam of the Age (PBUH) concerning the birth of Imam Husayn (PBUH) to Qasim ibn 'Ala' al-Hamadani.
sources: al-Isaba: vol. 1 p. 333. Tadhkirat al-Khawass of Ibn Jawzi: p. 134.
Translation of the biography of Imam Husayn (PBUH) from Ta'rikh Dimashq of Ibn 'Asakir: pp. 14-285.

events.title: Entry of Imam Husayn (PBUH) into Mecca
events.text: On the night of Friday, the 3rd of Sha'ban in the year 60 AH, Imam Husayn (PBUH) entered Mecca and stayed there until Dhu al-Hijja.
sources: Irshad: vol. 2 p. 35. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 338.

events.title: Birth of Hadrat Abbas (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 26 AH, the standard-bearer of Karbala, the water-bearer of Naynawa, Hadrat Qamar-e Munir of Banu Hashim (the Luminous Moon of Banu Hashim), Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas (PBUH) was born.
His famous name is Abbas (PBUH). He is called Abu al-Fadl, Abu al-Qirba, Qamar Bani Hashim, Bab al-Hawa'ij (Gate of Needs), 'Abd Salih (the Righteous Servant) and Saqqa (the Water-bearer). His father is Hadrat Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), and his mother is Hadrat Umm al-Banin Fatima (SA), daughter of Hizam al-Kilabiyya.
He was handsome and good-looking, and for this reason was titled the Moon of Banu Hashim. He had a tall stature and strong arms, and when he sat on a horse and placed his foot in the stirrup, his knees reached the horse's neck. He was a manifestation of the majesty and might of the Lord, and in courage and virtues, after Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (PBUT), he was foremost among the children of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH). He was the commander-in-chief and the oppressed standard-bearer of Karbala.
sources: Khasa'is al-'Abbasiyya: p. 66. Qamar Bani Hashim (PBUH) by Muqarram: p. 18. From Anis al-Shi'a. al-Waqa'i' wa al-Hawadith: vol. Muharram p. 400.
al-Abbas (PBUH): p. 164. The late Muqarram, citing historical sources, said that the title of Saqqa was his.

events.title: Birth of Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH)
events.text:
On this day in the year 38 AH, during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), our master and lord Hadrat Sayyid al-Sajidin Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH), son of al-Husayn (PBUH), was born.
His name is “Ali,” and his most famous blessed titles are Zayn al-Abidin and Sajjad. His father is the master of the martyrs Hadrat Aba Abdillah al-Husayn (PBUH), and his mother is Hadrat Shahrbanu.
Imam Sajjad (PBUH) spent two years of his blessed life with his grandfather the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), and the rest of his noble life was spent with his honored and oppressed uncle Imam Mujtaba (PBUH) and his exalted father Imam Husayn (PBUH). In the heart-rending event of Karbala he witnessed the martyrdom of his father, brother, uncle, relatives and companions (PBUT); together with his aunt Zaynab al-Kubra (SA) and the other captives he went to Kufa and Sham (Syria). In Kufa and Sham, insolences were committed against him and the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), but with luminous sermons he defended the Imamate and the infallibility of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT). In the palace of Yazid, while he and several others of the family of the Imamate were bound together with one rope, he turned to Yazid and said: “Ma zannuka bi-Rasulillah law ra'ana mawthuqina fi al-hibal...” — “O Yazid, what do you think of the Prophet if he were to see us bound in ropes like this?”
Other opinions about his birth are as follows: 8 Rabi' al-Awwal, 15 Jumada al-Ula, 15 Jumada al-Akhira, 5 Rajab, 11 Rajab, 7 Sha'ban, 9 Sha'ban, 15 Sha'ban, 5 Ramadan. There is also disagreement about the day of the week of his birth — whether it was Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday or Friday. There is also disagreement about the year of birth, whether it was 36, 37 or 38 AH.
sources: Kashf al-Ghumma: vol. 2 p. 74. Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 20.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 34. Usul al-Kafi: vol. 1 p. 467.
Sharh Ihqaq al-Haqq: vol. 19 p. 439. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Sha'ban, pp. 388-389.

events.title: Aqiqa for Imam Husayn (PBUH)
events.text: On this day, which is the seventh day after the birth of Imam Husayn (PBUH), the Messenger of God (SAWW) sacrificed a sheep as an aqiqa for his child. Then he shaved his head and gave silver in charity equal to the weight of his hair.
sources: Hayat al-Imam al-Husayn (PBUH): vol. 1 pp. 30-43. Irshad: vol. 2 p. 327. A'lam al-Wara: vol. 1 p. 420.

events.title: Decree (Tawqi') of the Imam of the Age (PBUH) for the Shi'a
events.text: On this day, Abu al-Hasan al-Samarri, six days before his passing, brought a decree (tawqi') from the sacred presence of Hadrat Sahib al-Amr (PBUH) for the Shi'a.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Sha'ban, p. 392. Waqa'i' al-Shuhur: p. 140.

events.title: Birth of Hadrat Ali Akbar (PBUH)
events.text:
In the year 33 AH, Hadrat Ali Akbar (PBUH), the person most resembling the Seal of the Prophets (SAWW), was born. His name is “Ali,” his father is Hadrat Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH), and his mother is Layla daughter of Murra al-Thaqafi. According to the statement of Hadrat Sadiq (PBUH), his kunya is “Aba al-Hasan.”
The narration of Bazanti also indicates that he was married. In the ziyara narrated from Hadrat Sadiq (PBUH) we also recite: “May God's blessings be upon you, and upon your progeny, your family, your fathers, your sons and your mothers, the good ones, from whom God has removed impurity and whom He has purified with a thorough purification.” The word “sons” (abna') in the ziyara indicates that he had even more than two children. At the event of Karbala, nearly 27 years of his blessed life had passed.
sources: Ali Akbar (PBUH) (Muqarram): pp. 15-16, citing Anis al-Shi'a.

events.title: Birth of Hadrat Baqiyyatullah al-A'zam (Peace of God be upon him)
events.text:
In the year 255 AH, on the night of Friday, the birth took place of the Seal of the Successors, the Avenger of the Family of Muhammad (SAWW), the last rightful Imam and absolute guardian of God, Hadrat Baqiyyatullah, Hujjat ibn al-Hasan (ATFS). On this night the water of Zamzam increases so much that everyone can see it, but now it is covered over. On this night the decree of freedom from the Fire is written for many people, and it is called the “Night of Bara'a (Absolution),” the “Blessed Night,” and the “Night of Mercy.”
It is narrated from Imam Baqir and Imam Sadiq (PBUT) that they said: When the night of mid-Sha'ban comes, a caller from the highest horizon calls out: “O visitors of the grave of Husayn ibn Ali, return, for your sins have been forgiven, and your reward is with your God and Muhammad.” But whoever is unable to visit the grave of Imam Husayn (PBUH) should visit the blessed graves of the other Imams; and if that is not possible either, he should send greetings by gesturing toward their graves.
The name of his father is Hadrat Abu Muhammad Hasan ibn Ali (PBUH), and the name of his mother is Hadrat Narjis (SA).
sources: Irshad: vol. 2 p. 339. A'lam al-Wara: vol. 2 p. 214. Kafi: vol. 1 p. 431. Masar al-Shi'a: p. 38. Tawdih al-Maqasid: pp. 20-21. Misbah al-Mutahajjid: p. 782. Misbah of Kaf'ami: vol. 2 p. 598. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 346. Jala' al-'Uyun: p. 579.
Taqwim al-Wa'izin p. 136. Citing Khulasat al-Minhaj: vol. 5 pp. 145-246.
Masar al-Shi'a: p. 38. Tawdih al-Maqasid: pp. 20-21. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 343.

subsections.title: The Story of the Night of the Birth
subsections.text:
On the night of the birth, Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH) sent a message to his honorable aunt Lady Hakima Khatun (SA), saying: Break your fast with us tonight, for it is the night of mid-Sha'ban, and God will reveal His Proof (Hujjat).
The birth of the Imam of the Age (PBUH) took place in the city of Samarra at the time of dawn on mid-Sha'ban of the year 255 AH. On his right shoulder was written: “Truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish.”
After his birth, he was brought to his father and began to speak: “I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that Ali is the Commander of the Faithful and the guardian of God,” and he named the Infallible Imams (PBUT) one after another until he reached his own noble self, and prayed for the relief of those who love him.

subsections.title: The Imam of the Age (PBUH) in His Father's Embrace
subsections.text:
Then, by order of Imam Askari (PBUH), Hakima Khatun took him to his mother Narjis Khatun. Hakima Khatun says: On the seventh day I went into the presence of Imam Hasan (PBUH). He said: “Bring my son.” We brought that generous being to the Imam. He placed his tongue in the child's mouth and said: “My son, speak.” I saw that he repeated what I had heard from him on the first day, the declaration of God's oneness and praise of his grandfather the Prophet (SAWW), the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) and the other Imams (PBUT), up to his honorable father, and he recited this verse: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful: “And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land, and make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and establish them in the land, and show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts what they feared from them.”
Then his honorable father said: Recite what God sent down upon His prophets. He began by reading the Scrolls of Adam in the Syriac language, and then recited the books of Idris, Noah, Salih, the Scrolls of Abraham, the Torah of Moses, the Gospel of Jesus, the Psalms of David and the Furqan of Muhammad (SAWW). After that he began relating the stories of the prophets and messengers. Hakima Khatun says: After forty more days, I again went into the presence of the son of my brother, Imam Askari (PBUH), and saw Hadrat Sahib al-Zaman (PBUH) walking. Imam Askari (PBUH) said: O aunt, this is the child dear to God. I said: O my master and lord, I see his growth in forty days to be more than that of others. He said: O aunt, we the successors grow in one day as others grow in a week, and in one week as others grow in a year. I stood up, kissed the child's head and returned home.

subsections.title: Titles of the Imam of the Age (PBUH)
subsections.text: Among the titles of that divine light are: “Hujjatullah” (the Proof of God), “Hujjat Al Muhammad” (the Proof of the Family of Muhammad), “Sahib al-Zaman” (the Master of the Age), meaning the ruler of his era, “Malik Riqab al-Khala'iq” (Master of the Necks of Creation), meaning his command is the command, his prohibition is the prohibition, his rule is the rule, and his order is the order; “Mahdi” (the Guided One), through whom creation is guided, and through whose sacred being they reach the highway of guidance from the road of misguidance and are saved; “Qa'im” (the One Who Rises), of whom Hadrat Sadiq (PBUH) said: “He is called Qa'im because he rises with the truth”; and “Muntazar” (the Awaited One), for whom there is a long occultation, and his sincere followers await his emergence while the doubters deny him.
sources: Kifayat al-Muwahhidin: vol. 3 p. 343. Kamal al-Din of Saduq: vol. 2 pp. 49, 159.

subsections.title: Attributes of the Imam of the Age (PBUH)
subsections.text: His outward attributes bear many similarities to the noble Messenger of Islam (SAWW). A line of emerald-green hair extends from his neck to his blessed navel. His blessed face is luminous like a shining star. The Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) says: “He is a handsome young man with beautiful hair, and the light of his blessed face shines over the blackness of his radiant beard, and he is victorious.” Imam Baqir (PBUH) says: “His blessed complexion inclines to redness, like a blossomed red rose; his eyes are wide, the space between his eyebrows is raised, and he is broad between his shoulders. He has a wide forehead, a tall and thin nose, a slight protrusion of his blessed belly, and a gap at the roots of his front teeth (thanaya).”

subsections.title: The Mother of the Imam of the Age (PBUH)
subsections.text:
The mother of Hadrat Sahib al-Amr (PBUH) is Hadrat Narjis Khatun, whose other names and titles are Hadrat Mulayka, Rayhana, Saqil and Sawsan. In her ziyara, all of whose phrases clearly indicate the high station of this lady, she is described as Radiya (content), Mardiyya (pleasing), Siddiqa (truthful), Taqiyya (pious), Naqiyya (pure) and Zakiyya (chaste).
According to one account, Lady Narjis passed away in Samarra in the year 261 AH and was buried beside the two Imams, Hadrat Hadi and Imam Askari (PBUT). According to another account, she passed away in the year 260 AH, before the martyrdom of Imam Askari (PBUH), because when the Imam (PBUH) informed her about the events after his martyrdom concerning his son and family, Lady Narjis Khatun (SA) asked him to pray that she would depart from the world before him.
Hadrat Hakima Khatun is the daughter of Hadrat Jawad al-A'imma (PBUH) and had the honor of seeing and living with four Infallible Imams (PBUT). She passed away in Samarra in the year 274 AH.
She was a confidante of the secrets of the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT) and was present at the birth of Hadrat Sahib al-Zaman (PBUH), and was honored to meet him several times. After the death of Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH), she was one of the envoys through whom people had their needs fulfilled.
sources: Ta'rikh Samarra': vol. 1 p. 243. Mustadrak Safinat al-Bihar: vol. 10 p. 25.

subsections.title: The Days After the Birth of the Imam of the Age (PBUH)
subsections.text:
One night after the birth of the Imam of the Age (PBUH), the servant Nasim came into his presence and sneezed. The Imam (PBUH) said: “May God have mercy on you.” Then he said: “A sneeze is security from death for three days.” This story is also narrated for the 25th of Sha'ban.
Three days after the birth of the Imam of the Age (PBUH), Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH) showed his son to his close companions and confirmed his Imamate.

subsections.title: The Minor Occultation (Ghayba Sughra)
subsections.text:
During the Minor Occultation, four of the great figures of the Shi'a were, in succession, the agent, ambassador and special deputy of the Imam of the Age (PBUH). They would be admitted into his presence, their agency was confirmed by him, and the Imam's (PBUH) replies in the margins of letters reached the people through the deputies.
Of course, apart from these four there were other agents appointed by the Imam (PBUH) in various lands, who conveyed people's affairs to the Imam of the Age (PBUH) through these four honorable men, and decrees (tawqi'at) had been issued by the Imam (PBUH) regarding their affairs. The embassy of these four was absolute and complete, whereas the others had embassy in specific matters, such as Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi, Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ash'ari, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani and Ahmad ibn Hamza ibn al-Yasa'.
The four deputies (Nuwwab Arba'a) are: Abu Amr Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri, Abu al-Qasim Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti, and Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri.
The first deputy, Uthman ibn Sa'id, was trusted by the people, of great stature, and was also the agent of Hadrat Hadi and Imam Askari (PBUT). By order of the Imam (PBUH) he took charge of the shrouding and burial of Imam Askari (PBUH). Since Imam Askari (PBUH) lived in the Askar quarter and contact with him was difficult for the Shi'a, Uthman ibn Sa'id, who was an oil seller, would pour the funds into oil containers and carry them to the Imam (PBUH).
When Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Qummi asked Imam Hadi (PBUH): My master, sometimes I am absent and sometimes present. And even when I am present I cannot always come into your presence. Whose word should we accept and whose command should we obey? The Imam said: This Abu Amr Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri is trustworthy and reliable; whatever he tells you, he says from me, and whatever he conveys to you, he conveys from me.
Ahmad ibn Ishaq says: After the passing of Imam Hadi (PBUH), I went to Imam Askari (PBUH) and repeated the same statement. Like his honorable father, he said: Abu Amr is trustworthy and reliable to the previous Imam, and he is trustworthy to me in my life and after my death. Whatever he tells you and whatever he conveys to you, he conveys from me.
After Imam Askari (PBUH), Uthman ibn Sa'id continued in agency and deputyship by order of Hadrat Mahdi (PBUH), and the Shi'a took their questions to him and the Imam's (PBUH) answers reached the people through him.
The second deputy was Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman, who like his father was one of the great figures of the Shi'a and was trusted and respected by the Shi'a for his piety, justice and nobility. Before his death, Uthman ibn Sa'id, by order of the Imam of the Age (PBUH), introduced his son Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman as his successor and as the Imam's (PBUH) deputy. This was while Imam Askari (PBUH) had expressed trust and confidence in him and his father, and the Shi'a were united on his justice, piety and obedience.
After the passing of the first deputy, Uthman ibn Sa'id, a decree (tawqi') was issued from the Imam of the Age (PBUH) regarding his death and the deputyship of his son Muhammad, part of which translates as follows: “Indeed we belong to God and to Him we return; we submit to the command of God and are content with His decree. Your father lived fortunate and passed away approved. May God have mercy on him and join him to his leaders and masters (PBUT). It was part of your father's complete good fortune that God granted him a son like you, to succeed him, to take his place in his affairs, and to seek mercy and forgiveness for him.”
Muhammad ibn Uthman was asked: Have you seen Sahib al-Amr (PBUH)? He said: Yes, and my last meeting with him was beside the Sacred House of God (Bayt Allah al-Haram), where he was saying: “O God, fulfill for me what You promised me.” I also saw him at al-Mustajar near the Yemeni Corner of the Ka'ba, saying: “O God, take vengeance for me upon my enemies.”
This honorable man composed books on jurisprudence containing what he had heard from Imam Askari (PBUH) and from his father.
Muhammad ibn Uthman had prepared a grave for himself and covered it with teak wood, and wrote verses of the noble Qur'an and the names of the pure Imams (PBUT) upon it. Every day he would enter it, recite one juz' of the Qur'an and come out. Before his death he announced the day of his own passing, and he died on the very day he had announced. Also before his passing he informed the Shi'a that the Imam (PBUH) had chosen Abu al-Qasim Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti for embassy and communication with himself, and that he was his successor, so they should refer to him. He passed away in the year 305 AH.
The third deputy is Abu al-Qasim Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti, who held special greatness among both friend and foe, and was famous for his intellect, insight, piety and virtue among all the various religious groups, and in the time of the second deputy was in charge of some affairs on his behalf.
Although among the companions of the second deputy Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Matil was closer to him than all others, and even in the last part of Muhammad ibn Uthman's life his food was prepared in the house of Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Matil, and among the companions the likelihood of Ja'far ibn Ahmad's deputyship and succession was greater, in the last hours of Muhammad ibn Uthman's life, when Ja'far ibn Ahmad was sitting at his head and Husayn ibn Ruh at his feet, he turned to Ja'far ibn Ahmad and said: “I have been commanded to entrust the affairs to Abu al-Qasim Husayn ibn Ruh.” Ja'far ibn Ahmad rose, took Husayn ibn Ruh's hand, seated him at the head of Muhammad ibn Uthman, and sat himself at his feet.
On the 6th of Shawwal in the year 305 AH, the first decree (tawqi') from the sacred presence of the Imam of the Age (PBUH) was issued for him, the text of which was as follows: “We know him; may God make known to him all His good and pleasure, and assist him with His grace. We have been informed of his letter and we have trust and confidence in him. He has a place and rank with us that pleases him. May God increase His favor to him, for God is the Guardian and Powerful over all things, and praise be to God who has no partner, and abundant blessings and peace of God be upon His Messenger Muhammad and his family, God's blessings be upon them.” Abu Sahl al-Nawbakhti, the author of works and one of the great theologians of Baghdad, was asked: Why did Abu al-Qasim Husayn ibn Ruh attain the station of deputyship and you did not? He said: The Imams (PBUT) know best, and what they choose is more fitting and more appropriate; but I am a person who confronts and debates the opponent, and if I were the Imam's (PBUH) deputy and knew the location of the Imam of the Age (PBUH) as Abu al-Qasim Husayn ibn Ruh knows it by virtue of his deputyship, and in the heat of debate about the Imam (PBUH) with opponents I were put in a tight spot, it is possible I could not control myself and would reveal the Imam's place; but Abu al-Qasim, even if the Imam (PBUH) were hidden beneath his skirt and they cut him to pieces with sharp instruments, he would not lift his skirt from him and would not show him to the enemy. Husayn ibn Ruh held the station of deputyship for about 21 years. Before his death, by order of the Imam (PBUH), he handed the affairs of deputyship to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri, and he passed away in the month of Sha'ban of the year 326 AH. His resting place is in Baghdad. The fourth deputy is Abu al-Hasan al-Samarri, to whom, by order of Hadrat Sahib al-Zaman (PBUH) to Husayn ibn Ruh, deputyship after him was entrusted. According to the great scholars of rijal, his greatness and exalted rank need no description. One day Abu al-Hasan al-Samarri said to a group of elders who were with him: “May God grant you reward in the calamity of Ali ibn Babawayh al-Qummi. At this very hour he has departed from the world.” They noted down the hour, day and month, and 17 or 18 days later news came that Ali ibn Babawayh al-Qummi had died at that very hour.
sources: Bihar al-Anwar: vol. 51 p. 346. al-Mahdi (PBUH): p. 181.

subsections.title: End of the Minor Occultation
subsections.text:
Before the passing of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri, a group of Shi'a gathered around him and asked: “Who will be your successor after you?” He replied: I have not been commanded to make a bequest to anyone in this matter. Then he showed the Shi'a a decree (tawqi') that had been issued by the Hidden Imam (PBUH) on this subject. They copied it down, and its content was as follows: “In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. O Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri, may God magnify the reward of your brothers in your bereavement, and make no bequest to anyone to succeed you. The Major Occultation has occurred, and there will be no reappearance until God Almighty gives the command, which will be after a long time, the hardening of hearts, and the earth being filled with oppression. Soon there will come to my Shi'a those who claim to have seen me. Beware: whoever claims this before the rising of the Sufyani and before the Cry (Sayha) (meaning claims to have seen me as a form of embassy and deputyship) is a liar and a fabricator, and there is no power and no strength except with God, the Most High, the Most Great.”
On the sixth day, which coincided with mid-Sha'ban of the year 329 AH, Abu al-Hasan al-Samarri passed away, and was buried on Khalanji Street beside the Abu Attab canal in Baghdad.
Majlisi (RA) narrates from the Ihtijaj of the late Shaykh Tabarsi: None of the special deputies of the Imam of the Age (PBUH) undertook the deputyship except by the explicit command of that Imam, and the appointment, installation and introduction by the previous deputy. The Shi'a also did not accept the word of any of them except after the appearance, at the hands of each of them, of a sign and miracle from the Imam of the Age (PBUH) which indicated the truth of his words and the soundness of his deputyship.
sources: The rising of the Sufyani and the Cry (Sayha) are two of the signs that will occur at the time of the reappearance of the Imam of the Age (PBUH).

subsections.title: Duties During the Time of the Major Occultation
subsections.text:
The Shi'a and friends of the Imam have duties during the time of the occultation, among them:
1. Reciting the Du'a Nudba on Fridays, Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Ghadir.
2. Visiting (ziyara of) the Imam on Fridays.
3. For firmness and steadfastness of belief, reciting this noble supplication: Ya Allah, Ya Rahman, Ya Rahim, Ya Muqallib al-Qulub, thabbit qalbi ala dinik (O God, O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful, O Turner of Hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion).
4. Standing up out of respect when the name “Qa'im” of that honorable one is mentioned.
5. Seeking his intercession (tawassul) in difficulties and hardships.
6. Giving charity for the health and relief (faraj) of his noble being.
7. Reciting this supplication in which we ask God to make us know him: Allahumma arrifni nafsak fa-innaka in lam tu'arrifni nafsaka lam a'rif nabiyyak, Allahumma arrifni rasulak fa-innaka in lam tu'arrifni rasulaka lam a'rif hujjatak, Allahumma arrifni hujjatak fa-innaka in lam tu'arrifni hujjataka dalaltu an dini (O God, make Yourself known to me, for if You do not make Yourself known to me I will not know Your Prophet; O God, make Your Messenger known to me, for if You do not make Your Messenger known to me I will not know Your Proof; O God, make Your Proof known to me, for if You do not make Your Proof known to me I will go astray from my religion).
8. Participating in gatherings attributed to him, especially the mourning gatherings for his honorable grandfather Hadrat Sayyid al-Shuhada (PBUH).
9. Dedicating righteous deeds as gifts to him, such as visiting the blessed graves of his honorable forefathers, reciting the Qur'an, Hajj, Umra and tawaf.
10. Sincere repentance from sins.
11. Directing people's attention to him.

events.title: Passing of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri, Deputy of the Imam of the Age (PBUH)
events.text: The passing of the eminent shaykh and special deputy of the Imam of the Age (PBUH), Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samarri, was on this day, which means the end of the Minor Occultation and the beginning of the Major Occultation, since Hadrat Sahib al-Amr (PBUH) had commanded him not to appoint any successor or deputy for himself, because the Major Occultation had begun.
sources: Haqq al-Yaqin: p. 301. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1 p. 375. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 348. Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Sha'ban, p. 463.

events.title: Passing of Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti, Deputy of the Imam of the Age (PBUH)
events.text: On this day in the year 326 AH, the third deputy of Hadrat Sahib al-Amr (ATFS), Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nawbakhti, departed to the world of eternity in Baghdad and was buried there.
sources: Qala'id al-Nuhur: vol. Sha'ban p. 463. For more details see the 15th of Sha'ban.

events.title: Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq
events.text:
On this day in the year 6 AH, the expedition (ghazwa) of Banu al-Mustaliq took place.
The march for this war began on the 2nd of Sha'ban of the same year. The number of Muslims was 1000, who had 30 horses, whereas the unbelievers numbered 700. One Muslim was martyred in this war and 10 of the unbelievers were killed. In this war victory and triumph belonged to the Muslims. Mustaliq is a station between Mecca and Medina which is named after Mustaliq. He was the first person to alter the religion of Ishmael (PBUH), and he commanded his tribe to worship Hubal and installed it in the Ka'ba.
sources: Tawdih al-Maqasid: p. 21. Fayd al-'Allam: p. 349.
al-Mawsu'a al-Kubra fi Ghazawat al-Nabi al-A'zam (SAWW): vol. 3 p. 12.

events.title: Death of Hafsa
events.text:
In the month of Sha'ban in the year 45 AH, Hafsa died and Marwan led the prayer over her body. Hafsa, daughter of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, was at first the wife of Khunays ibn Abdullah. After Khunays died, 'Umar gave her in marriage to the Prophet (SAWW). With her character and conduct she used to harm the Prophet (SAWW) and the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), to such an extent that the Prophet (SAWW) divorced her and then took her back at the insistence of some.
In the Battle of Jamal she wanted to set out with Aisha, but her brother Abdullah ibn 'Umar prevented her. But when the army of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) reached the station of Dhi Qar, Aisha wrote a letter to Hafsa to this effect: “The news of the great number of our army has reached Ali ibn Abi Talib (PBUH), and out of fear he has halted at Dhi Qar, and he will not escape this war alive...”
When the letter reached Hafsa, she gathered maidservants and singing-girls, who played tambourines and recited verses in which they spoke ill of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), and the women of Banu Umayya gathered and made merry.
When the news reached Umm Kulthum (SA), she and a number of women entered the gathering unrecognized and suddenly uncovered their faces. Hafsa was ashamed. Umm Kulthum (SA) recited to Hafsa the verse concerning the wives of Noah and Lot (PBUT), who disobeyed those two prophets, which was revealed about Hafsa and Aisha, and said: If today you and Aisha are helping each other to humiliate my father the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), this deed of yours is nothing new, for you did the same to my grandfather the Prophet (SAWW). When Hafsa saw that she had been disgraced, she tore up Aisha's letter and asked Umm Kulthum (SA) not to disgrace her any further.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari: vol. 3 p. 103, vol. 6 p. 148. Musnad Ahmad: vol. 1 pp. 33-34. Sahih Muslim: vol. 4 p. 193. Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 14 p. 23.

Surat al-Tahrim: verse 10: “God sets forth, as an example for those who disbelieve, the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them, so they availed them nothing against God, and it was said: Enter the Fire with those who enter.”
Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 14 p. 13.

events.title: The Prophet's (SAWW) Expedition Against Banu Sa'd
events.text: In Sha'ban of the sixth year of the Hijra, the Prophet (SAWW) sent the Commander of the Faithful Ali (PBUH) with 100 men to confront the tribe of Banu Sa'd in the vicinity of Medina. Banu Sa'd, having been informed, fled, and the Muslims took one hundred camels and one thousand sheep as spoils. The Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) set aside some camels for the Prophet (SAWW), distributed the other spoils among the Muslims, and they returned to Medina.

events.title: Martyrdom of Sa'id ibn Jubayr
events.text:
In this month in the year 95 AH, Sa'id ibn Jubayr al-Kufi was martyred at the hands of Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi. Sa'id was a jurist, ascetic and devout worshipper who had the honor of acquiring knowledge in the blessed presence of Hadrat Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH). Because of his pure faith and complete love for the Infallible Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), he enjoyed special respect with Imam Zayn al-Abidin (PBUH).
When Hajjaj wanted to martyr that great man, he prayed that after his martyrdom Hajjaj would be unable to kill anyone. God answered his prayer, and Hajjaj lived 15 to 20 days after the martyrdom of Sa'id and killed no one, until he went to his doom from the disease of akila (a flesh-eating ailment).
After Hajjaj severed the head of that great man, they also cut off his two blessed legs at the shins. He was 57 or 79 years of age, and was buried in the city of al-Hayy in Wasit, Iraq. The grave of that great man is one of the pilgrimage sites of those who love the Ahl al-Bayt (PBUT), and has a dome and a large courtyard with four gates.
Some have narrated the death of Hajjaj as 15 days, some 20 days and some 40 days after the martyrdom of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, so that if the death of Hajjaj was on the 13th of Ramadan, the martyrdom of Sa'id is probable, respectively, on the 27th, 28th, 22nd or 23rd, and 2nd or 3rd of Sha'ban; but what is certain is that the martyrdom of Sa'id was in Sha'ban.
sources: Sa'id ibn Jubayr: pp. 25-29. Muntakhab al-Tawarikh: p. 423. Maraqid al-Ma'arif: vol. 1 pp. 351-352.

events.title: Death of Mughira ibn Shu'ba
events.text:
In the month of Sha'ban in the year 50 AH, Mughira ibn Shu'ba, while serving as governor of Kufa on behalf of Mu'awiya, went to his doom at the age of 70, and Ziyad ibn Abihi was appointed in his place. In Kufa, Mughira cursed the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH) and ordered the preachers to curse him, and did not abandon this practice until the time of his death.
Mughira was among the companions of the accursed Sahifa and of the Night of Aqaba, who wanted to kill the Prophet (SAWW), and he was also among the companions of the Saqifa.
He was among those who took part in setting fire to the house of the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), breaking the door, striking the Mother of the Sayyids, Hadrat Siddiqa Shahida Fatima al-Zahra (SA), and the miscarriage.
The adultery of Mughira with Umm Jamil in Basra is especially well known and is recorded in Shi'a and Sunni books with various documents. Ibn Abi al-Hadid says: Mughira was the most adulterous of people in the Jahiliyya and in Islam. Mughira was among those who, by order of Mu'awiya, together with Amr ibn al-As and Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, fabricated false narrations whose implication was the obligation of cursing and dissociating from the Commander of the Faithful (PBUH), and for this work Mu'awiya set extraordinary rewards for them. He committed insolences against his honorable father in the presence of Imam Hasan (PBUH). But the Imam gave him fitting answers and at the end said: “You are the one who was a partner in the martyrdom of my mother and my brother Muhsin (PBUT)...”
sources: Kashf al-Hawiya: p. 288. Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 2 p. 102.
Sharh Ibn Abi al-Hadid: vol. 1 p. 358.
